message.content:
The three most widely‑recognized “great schisms” in Christian history are:

| # | Schism | Year | Key Parties | Main Issue |
|---|--------|------|-------------|------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism (East–West Schism)** | 1054 | Roman Catholic Church (West) vs. Eastern Orthodox Church (East) | Diverging theological, liturgical, and political practices; the mutual excommunication of the Patriarch of Constantinople and the Pope. |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 | Roman Catholic Church vs. various Protestant movements (Lutheran, Calvinist, Anglican, etc.) | Critique of papal authority, indulgences, and other church practices; led to the creation of numerous Protestant denominations. |
| 3 | **East–West Schism of 1969 (also called the “Second Great Schism” in some contexts)** | 1969 | Roman Catholic Church vs. the Old Catholic Church (and other independent Catholic groups) | Disputes over the authority of the Pope, the nature of the sacraments, and the role of the Vatican in doctrinal matters. |

These three events are often cited as the major ruptures that reshaped the structure, theology, and global distribution of Christianity.
